title: DNS-over-HTTPS accepts untrusted certificates

evidence.quoted_code:
82: 	httpClient := doh.NewHttpClient(
83: 		doh.WithTimeout(options.Timeout),
84: 		doh.WithInsecureSkipVerify(),
85: 		doh.WithProxy(options.Proxy), // no-op if empty
86: 	)

source: Operator-selected DoH resolver; DNS data returned over an attacker-intercepted connection.
path: -r doh:https://... enters Options.Resolvers
runner.New -> dnsx.New -> retryabledns.NewWithOptions
DoH client disables TLS chain/hostname validation
QueryOne/QueryMultiple accepts DNS answers from that connection
why_exploitable: An on-path party can impersonate the selected DoH service with an untrusted certificate and forge DNS results. This affects the encrypted DoH mode; UDP defaults are a separate, intentionally unencrypted mode.
preconditions: DoH is explicitly configured; attacker can intercept traffic or impersonate its endpoint. No additional certificate pinning was found on this path.
challenge_verdict: CONFIRMED. Default Go HTTPS rejects the local self-signed server; actual DNSX accepted its 192.0.2.123 answer. DoT is a different transport and was not flagged.
how_to_verify: Run TestAuditDoHSelfSigned. It uses httptest.NewTLSServer on loopback and audit.test; baseline HTTPS must reject the certificate, and the patched DNSX must reject it too.
first_introduced: Not established; this audit dates observation, not introduction.

title: Automatic version-check client disables TLS verification
source: Remote version metadata and network path to api.pdtm.sh.
path: ParseOptions performs version check unless -duc
GetToolVersionCallback requests HTTPS version metadata
DefaultHttpClient accepts untrusted TLS certificates
why_exploitable: An on-path party can forge the reported latest version or observe transmitted machine/tool metadata. This is not evidence of replacement-binary execution: the release downloader uses a different path.
preconditions: Automatic version check enabled (default), and attacker controls the network path or a configured interception proxy.
challenge_verdict: DOWNGRADED to Low. Self-signed acceptance reproduced. The insecure client is documented as version-check-only, so a claim of arbitrary malicious update installation through this client was rejected.
how_to_verify: Run TestAuditVersionTLS against a loopback self-signed server. After changing the TLS configuration, this request must fail certificate verification. Use -duc as an immediate workaround.
first_introduced: Not established; this audit dates observation, not introduction.
fix_diff:
--- utils/update/update.go
+++ utils/update/update.go
@@
-			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true},
+			TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: false},

path: -testcases selects a file

title: Stdin temporary-file creation loses atomicity and privacy
source: Piped scan input and the filesystem entry in the temporary directory.
sink: os.Create of a filename returned after its original file was deleted.
path: GetTempFileName creates a safe temporary file
helper closes and deletes it, returning only its name
runner reopens that name with os.Create
stdin bytes are copied to the reopened path
why_exploitable: The create-delete-recreate gap allows a replacement symlink to redirect truncation and stdin writes where filesystem policy permits. os.Create also uses 0666 before umask, unlike CreateTemp's 0600, making scan input world-readable under umask 022.
preconditions: Non-stream piped stdin path is used. Reading requires access to the temp directory under a permissive umask; redirecting writes additionally requires winning the gap and passing OS symlink protections. Linux protected_symlinks can block cross-user attacks in sticky directories.
challenge_verdict: CONFIRMED unsafe sequence and controlled interleaving, not a measured natural race. Existing CreateTemp randomness was considered: deletion removes its atomic protection. Severity is conditional; same-user reproduction does not prove cross-user privilege escalation.
how_to_verify: Run TestAuditTempRace: real helper returns a removed name; insert a symlink to a temporary victim, then reproduce os.Create. Keep the CreateTemp descriptor instead. Verify mode is 0600 and no reopen gap remains.
first_introduced: Not established; this audit dates observation, not introduction.
fix_diff:
--- internal/runner/runner.go
+++ internal/runner/runner.go
@@
-		tmpStdinFile, err := fileutil.GetTempFileName()
+		stdinFile, err := os.CreateTemp("", "dnsx-stdin-*")
 		if err != nil { return err }
-		r.tmpStdinFile = tmpStdinFile
-		stdinFile, err := os.Create(r.tmpStdinFile)
-		if err != nil { return err }
+		r.tmpStdinFile = stdinFile.Name()
+		defer os.Remove(r.tmpStdinFile)
+		defer stdinFile.Close()
# Keep io.Copy and its error check; replace the later RemoveAll defer.

17:       - uses: projectdiscovery/actions/goreleaser@v1

source: Remote third-party action code addressed by @v1/@v3/@v4/@v5.
sink: GitHub Actions execution with write permissions or release/deployment secrets.
path: Successful compatibility run can trigger auto-merge job
job has contents/pull-requests write
mutable projectdiscovery action tags select executable code
release and Docker jobs also execute tagged actions with secrets
why_exploitable: A moved or compromised action tag changes executed code without a reviewed workflow change. The auto-merge job explicitly has write permissions; release and Docker steps have sensitive credentials in their jobs. No action compromise was observed.
preconditions: Attacker must control an action repository/tag or its publishing account, and the workflow must run. Actual token defaults and action behavior depend on repository settings and remote code not supplied.
challenge_verdict: CONFIRMED references and privilege grants, not confirmed compromise. workflow_run alone was not treated as a fork-code takeover; external approve/merge internals and branch rules remain unverified.
how_to_verify: Resolve each action version to a reviewed full 40-character commit SHA, pin it, and use automated reviewed updates. Run CI on an owned test repository and verify only intended permissions are available.
first_introduced: Not established; this audit dates observation, not introduction.
fix_diff:
No guessed SHAs are supplied. Replace each uses: owner/action@tag
with its independently verified full commit SHA (optionally comment
the release tag), starting with approve/merge and release/deploy jobs.
Set permissions: contents: read by default; grant only the necessary
job-specific write scopes. Review third-party action code before pinning.

title: Docker publication is not bound to a successful release commit

evidence.quoted_code:
3: on:
4:   workflow_run:
5:     workflows: ["🎉 Release Binary"]
6:     types:
7:       - completed
8:   workflow_dispatch:
9: 
10: jobs:
11:   docker:
12:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest-16-cores
13:     steps:
14:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
15: 
16:       - name: Get Github tag
17:         id: meta
18:         run: |
19:           curl --silent "https://api.github.com/repos/projectdiscovery/dnsx/releases/latest" | jq -r .tag_name | xargs -I {} echo TAG={} >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

29:       - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
30:         with:
31:           context: .
32:           platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/arm
33:           push: true
34:           tags: projectdiscovery/dnsx:latest,projectdiscovery/dnsx:${{ steps.meta.outputs.TAG }}

source: Completed release workflow, default checkout ref, and latest-release API tag.
sink: Docker build and push tagged with independently fetched release metadata.
path: Any completed release workflow triggers Docker job, including failure
checkout has no release-associated ref
latest tag is fetched separately
build uses current checkout and publishes latest + fetched tag
why_exploitable: The workflow can publish on a failed release run, and the built commit is not constrained to the commit represented by its version tag. That can overwrite a versioned image with unrelated source, undermining reproducibility and audit traceability.
preconditions: Workflow deployed as supplied; a release run completes or manual dispatch starts the Docker workflow. Real mismatch depends on timing/default branch and repository release state.
challenge_verdict: CONFIRMED missing success/ref binding in configuration; actual mislabelled image was not verified because GitHub/Docker deployment access was not provided. This is an integrity issue, not demonstrated attacker RCE.
how_to_verify: In an owned test repository, simulate a failed release run and assert no push job runs. For success, assert image revision equals the triggering head_sha and tag metadata derives from that same immutable commit.
first_introduced: Not established; this audit dates observation, not introduction.
fix_diff:
--- .github/workflows/dockerhub-push.yml
+++ .github/workflows/dockerhub-push.yml
@@
   docker:
+    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'
@@
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
# Derive/validate the version tag from this checked-out commit, not
# /releases/latest. Require an explicit tag for manual dispatch.

title: Incomplete scans and output failures can appear successful

source: Invalid/missing input, zero/negative worker count, and output write failures.
sink: Discarded Run error, worker creation loop, buffered output flush/write.
path: No-input prepareInput returns empty argument error
main discards dnsxRunner.Run return

why_exploitable: Automation can receive exit status 0 for an empty-input failure or a run that resolves nothing. The actual output handler also returns normally when /dev/full rejects its deferred flush. That can cause incomplete or missing evidence to be mistaken for a completed audit.
preconditions: No input, nonpositive -t, or an output filesystem error. The /dev/full reproduction ran only in the isolated test handler. A CLI /dev/full attempt did not obtain a DNS answer, so it was excluded as proof of output-loss behavior.
challenge_verdict: CONFIRMED via actual CLI for no input and -t 0, both exit 0/no output; confirmed output-error discard via handler test. Negative retries/timeouts are not separately claimed without dependency validation analysis.
how_to_verify: Re-run recorded no_input and zero_threads checks; both should return nonzero with an actionable message after fixing. Run TestAuditOutputErrorDiscarded with explicit error propagation and expect a failure signal.
first_introduced: Not established; this audit dates observation, not introduction.

@@

title: Stream mode without stdin panics
source: Stream invocation with no file input and no piped stdin.
path: -stream is accepted without requiring stdin
InputWorkerStream initializes sc only for file or available stdin
with stdin redirected from /dev/null neither branch sets sc
sc.Scan dereferences nil and process exits 2
why_exploitable: A routine invocation error crashes the process with a stack trace rather than a controlled input-validation error. This is not a remotely reachable service crash in the supplied architecture.
preconditions: CLI is invoked with -stream and no piped input; normal CLI validation forbids a hosts flag in stream mode. A wrapper that allows this invocation can be disrupted.
challenge_verdict: CONFIRMED. dnsx -duc -silent -nc -stream </dev/null exited 2 with panic at runner.go:247. Treated as Low local availability impact, not remote DoS.
how_to_verify: Run that CLI command in a disposable environment. Patched code should produce a concise nonzero error without a panic; normal piped stream input must still work.
first_introduced: Not established; this audit dates observation, not introduction.
